[P5] 他从床上跳下来，一口气跑过漆黑的树林，来到小鸭的家门口。

“你跑来看我真好，”小鸭说，“但是现在很晚了，我正要上床睡觉呢！”
“求你了，小鸭！”弗洛格说，“我被吓坏了。有个鬼在我的床底下！”

[P6] “乱说！”小鸭大笑起来，“世界上根本没有这样的东西。”
“有！”小鸭说：“你可以待在我这里，我不怕。”然后他们缩成一团，窝在床上。弗洛格紧紧靠着小鸭温暖的身体，不再害怕了。

突然，他们听到屋顶上传来刷刷的摩擦声。“什么东西？”小鸭吓了一跳，从床上坐了起来。接着又听见楼梯上传来咔咔声。“这个房子也闹鬼了！”弗洛格大叫，“我们快出去吧！”他们逃进了树林里。

[P7] fú luó gé hé xiǎo yā pīn mìng de pǎo
弗洛格和小鸭拼命地跑。
tā men jué de dào chù dōu shì yǒu líng hé kě pà de guǐ wu
他们觉得到处都是幽灵和可怕的怪物。

[P8] 他们跑到小猪家，先深吸一口气，然后敲门。
“谁啊？”一个没睡醒的声音问。
“小猪，是我们！请你快开门。”弗洛格和小鸭大声叫着。

“怎么搞的？”小猪生气了，“你们干吗三更半夜把我吵起来？”
“请你帮帮我们！”小鸭说，“树林里到处都是幽灵和怪物，吓死我们了。”
小猪笑了：“不要乱说！鬼和怪物根本不存在，你们知道的。”
“那你自己看看好了。”弗洛格说。

[P9] 小猪往窗外望去，看不出有什么不对劲。“小猪，我们可不可以睡在你这里？我们很害怕。”“好吧！”小猪说，“我的床很大，我从来不怕，我才不信这些呢。”

于是他们三个挤在床上。“真好！”弗洛格心想，“这下可安全了。”可是他们都睡不着。他们听着所有来自树林里的奇怪又可怕的声音。这一次，就连小猪也听到了。

[P10] 还好，三个朋友可以互相安慰。他们一起大声喊着他们不怕——他们什么也不怕。最后，他们累得睡着了。

第二天早上，野兔去弗洛格家拜访。弗洛格家的大门开着，屋里没有他的踪影。

“这可真怪！”野兔心里想着。

[P11] 小鸭的家里也没有人。”小鸭，小鸭，你在哪儿？”野兔大叫着。但是没有人回答。野兔很担心，心想一定发生了什么可怕的事情。
野兔很害怕，赶忙跑到树林里找弗洛格和小鸭。找了又找，就是没有他们的踪影。“也许小猪知道他们在哪儿！”他想。

[P12] 野兔敲着小猪家的门，没有人应门。这时四周一片宁静。他从窗户往里看，看到他的三个朋友躺在床上睡得正香呢。已经上午十点钟了！野兔敲着窗子。

“救命啊！一个鬼！”三个朋友一起大叫起来。接着他们看清了窗外原来是野兔。

[P13] 小猪开了门，他们冲了出来。“哦，野兔！”他们说，“我们被吓坏了。树林里到处是可怕的鬼和吓人的怪物。”“鬼和怪物？”野兔很惊讶，“他们根本不存在。”

“你怎么知道？”弗洛格生气了，“我的床底下就有一个。”“你亲眼看到了吗？”野兔平平地问。“没有。”青蛙说。他没有看见过但听过。他们谈了很久很久有关鬼、怪物和其他恐怖的事情。

[P14] 小猪做了一些早餐。“你知道吗？”野兔说，“每个人都有害怕的时候。”“连你也会吗？”弗洛格惊讶地问。
“是的，”野兔说，“就在今天早上，我以为你们不见了的时候，简直吓坏了。大家有好一会儿都没有说话。”

[P15] 学会战胜恐惧
每个人都有害怕的时候，不过我们可以变得更勇敢些。如果你心里感到恐惧，就学着用一些方法来克服吧——有的方法真的很管用！

想一想
1. 青蛙为什么被吓坏了？
2. 野兔为什么被吓坏了？
3. 世界上有没有鬼和吓人的怪物？

试一试
你平时害怕什么？把你的害怕说出来，告诉爸爸妈妈或老好朋友，听听他们是怎么说的。

接着，他们一起大笑起来。“别傻了，野兔！”弗洛格说，“没什么好怕的，我们永远都会在。”

[P1] Author Max Velthuijs is a highly acclaimed children's illustrator internationally.
This series has won the Dutch Golden Pencil Award, the French Prix de Treize Award,
the German Bestlist Award, and the American Graphic Award.

"Like other stories, the simple and vivid illustrations make the story content even more wonderful— the picture of Frog running quickly through the forest is a true masterpiece."
—UK Children's Education

This is a series of psychological education stories that help children's emotional growth. Each story naturally reveals an important theme, full of imagination. The text and illustrations are both created by Max Velthuijs. The writing is lively and subtly humorous, while the illustrations feature a rare simple line-drawing style, hailed by Western artists as "a masterpiece of the world of simple drawings." The series has been translated into 38 languages and has sold over a million copies worldwide.

ISBN 7-5358-3062-5

ISBN 7-5358-3062-5/1·337
Price: 4.80 RMB

Frogger's Growth Stories
A psychological self-help gift for children in the critical period of personality development (ages 3-6)

Illustrations and Text / (Netherlands) Max Velthuijs
Frog is Scared
—Learning to Overcome Fear—

Hunan Children's Publishing House

[P2] Awarded
Hans Christian Andersen
Illustration Award
Frog and Toad's Growth Stories

Illustrations and Text / (Netherlands) Max Velthuijs
Frog is Scared
——Learning to Overcome Fear——

Hunan Children's Publishing House

[P5] He jumped out of bed and ran through the dark forest, arriving at Duck's front door.

"You came to see me, that's great," said Duck, "but it's very late now, I'm just about to go to bed!"
"Please, Duck!" said Frog, "I'm terrified. There's a ghost under my bed!"

[P6] "Nonsense!" the duck laughed. "There's no such thing in the world."
"There is!" the duck said. "You can stay here with me, I'm not afraid." Then they curled up together, snuggling in bed. Frog clung tightly to the duck's warm body and was no longer afraid.

Suddenly, they heard a brushing sound coming from the roof. "What's that?" the duck jumped, sitting up in bed. Then they heard a creaking sound coming from the stairs. "This house is haunted too!" Frog shouted, "Let's get out of here quickly!" They ran into the forest.

[P7] Frog and Duck are running for their lives.
They feel that ghosts and terrifying monsters are everywhere.

[P8] They ran to Pig's house, took a deep breath, and knocked on the door.
"Who is it?" a sleepy voice asked.
"Pig, it's us! Please open the door quickly!" Frog and Duck called out loudly.

"What's going on?" Pig got angry. "Why are you waking me up in the middle of the night?"
"Please help us!" Duck said. "There are ghosts and monsters everywhere in the forest, we're terrified!"
Pig laughed. "Don't be silly! Ghosts and monsters don't exist, you know that."
"Then you should check it out yourself," Frog said.

[P9] Pig looked out the window and couldn't see anything wrong. "Pig, can we sleep here? We're very scared." "Alright!" Pig said, "My bed is big, I've never been afraid, I don't believe in these things at all."

So the three of them squeezed onto the bed. "Great!" Frog thought, "This is safe now." But none of them could sleep. They listened to all the strange and frightening sounds coming from the woods. This time, even Pig heard them.

[P10] It's okay, the three friends can comfort each other. They shout together that they are not afraid — they are not afraid of anything. In the end, they fall asleep from exhaustion.

The next morning, the rabbit visits Frog's house. Frog's front door is open, but there is no sign of him inside.

"This is really strange!" the rabbit thinks to himself.

[P11] There was no one in Duck's house. "Duck, Duck, where are you?" Rabbit shouted. But no one answered. Rabbit was very worried, thinking something terrible must have happened.
Rabbit was very scared and hurried to the forest to look for Frog and Duck. He searched and searched, but couldn't find any trace of them. "Maybe Pig knows where they are!" he thought.

[P12] The rabbit knocked on Pig's door, but no one answered. The surroundings were quiet. He looked in through the window and saw his three friends sleeping soundly in bed. It was already ten o'clock in the morning! The rabbit knocked on the window.

"Help! A ghost!" the three friends screamed together. Then they saw clearly that it was the rabbit outside the window.

[P13] The pig opened the door, and they rushed out. "Oh, Rabbit!" they said, "We were scared to death. There are terrible ghosts and frightening monsters in the woods." "Ghosts and monsters?" Rabbit was surprised. "They don't exist at all."

"How do you know?" Frog got angry. "There's one under my bed!" "Did you see it with your own eyes?" Rabbit asked calmly. "No," said the frog. He hadn't seen it, but he had heard it. They talked for a long, long time about ghosts, monsters, and other scary things.

[P14] Pig made some breakfast. "Do you know?" said Rabbit, "Everyone has moments of fear." "Even you?" asked Frog, surprised.
"Yes," said Rabbit, "Just this morning, when I thought you had disappeared, I was absolutely terrified. We all sat in silence for a while."

[P15] Learning to Overcome Fear
Everyone has moments of fear, but we can become braver. If you feel afraid, try learning some ways to overcome it—some methods really work!

Think About It
1. Why was the frog scared?
2. Why was the rabbit scared?
3. Are there ghosts or scary monsters in the world?

Try This
What are you usually afraid of? Speak your fears out loud, tell your parents or a good friend, and listen to what they say.

Then, they all burst out laughing. “Don’t be silly, Rabbit!” said Frog. “There’s nothing to be afraid of. We’ll always be here.”

[P5] 弗洛格因害怕床底下的鬼而惊醒，从床上跳下，跑过漆黑的树林，来到小鸭家门口求助。小鸭开门后表示很晚了，正要睡觉，弗洛格则恳求他帮忙，说自己被床底下的鬼吓坏了。

[P8] 弗洛格和小鸭跑到小猪家求助，声称树林里到处都是幽灵和怪物，小猪不信，认为鬼怪不存在，弗洛格建议他亲自去看看。
[P9] 弗洛格、小鸭和小猪挤在小猪家的床上，虽然觉得安全，但都因听到树林里奇怪可怕的声音而无法入睡，连一向不信鬼怪的小猪也听到了声音。
[P10] 三个朋友在小猪家的床上睡着了，第二天早上野兔去弗洛格家拜访，发现门开着但屋里没人，感到奇怪。

[P13] 野兔来到小猪家，发现弗洛格、小鸭和小猪正在床上熟睡，便敲窗叫醒他们。三个朋友误以为是鬼，惊叫起来，随后发现是野兔。他们向野兔讲述了树林里鬼怪的恐怖经历，野兔表示鬼怪不存在，但弗洛格坚持床底下有鬼，他们于是讨论了很久关于鬼怪和恐怖的事情。

[P15] 本页展示了朋友们在经历恐惧后互相安慰并大笑起来的场景，同时通过文字引导读者思考恐惧的来源，并提供克服恐惧的方法。
